text:
lucy.k: Hi all, new joiner here. My first pipeline run in redwood/ml-tools fails on the artifact upload step with a 403. Anyone know the usual onboarding snag?

buildkite-bot: Build #7 failed - step: upload-artifacts (exit code: 1)
```
Uploading artifacts...
Response: 403 Forbidden
POST https://api.github.com/repos/redwood/ml-tools/releases/123/assets -> 403
```

marco: Welcome! 403 usually means the token used for GH uploads doesn't have repo scope or the Buildkite app lacks permissions. Did you see RELEASE_TOKEN or a pipeline secret configured?

lucy.k: I didn't set any token, assumed the pipeline would have one. Where should that live?

ci-oncall-bot: Reminder: new hires should request a release-bot token via #eng-infra or use the release-operator identity. Avoid creating long-lived personal tokens.

marco: I'll generate a temporary scoped bot token and add it to the pipeline secrets. @infra-team can rotate it after Lucy replaces with the production release-operator.

infra-team: Token added to pipeline as SECRET_RELEASE_TOKEN (masked). Please re-run the failed job.

lucy.k: Re-ran the job — upload step now shows 201 Created. Thanks!

marco: Follow-ups: I'll add a quick note to onboarding docs: check RELEASE_TOKEN or release-operator steps. Also we should add a pipeline check to fail early if token missing.

lucy.k: Great, appreciate the fast help. Happy to update docs once I find the doc location.

buildkite-bot: Build #7 (re-run) passed - step: upload-artifacts
